The '''1997–98 Scottish Premier Division''' season was the last season of [[Scottish Football League Premier Division]] football before the change to the [[Scottish Premier League]]. It began on 1 August 1997.

==Overview==
The 1997–98 Scottish Premier Division season ended in success for [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] who won by two points from nearest rivals [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]], beating [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] on the last day to clinch the title. Claiming the trophy would have given Rangers a [[Nine in a row|record-breaking 10 Scottish League Championships in a row]] (having matched Celtic's record the previous season). [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] ran Celtic and Rangers very close to winning the title, and led for large spells of the season before falling away towards the end of the season. [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] were relegated to the [[Scottish First Division|First Division]] after finishing bottom. As champions, Celtic qualified for the [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] while Rangers were joined by [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] in qualifying for the [[UEFA Cup]]. Third-placed [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] qualified for the last [[UEFA Cup Winners' Cup|Cup Winners' Cup]] as [[Scottish Cup]] winners.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.soccerbot.com/scot/results/sdprem98.htm|title=1997/98 Scottish Premier Division|publisher=Soccerbot|access-date=2008-06-03|archive-date=2008-10-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081007064850/http://www.soccerbot.com/scot/results/sdprem98.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Rangers were involved in some of the season's big transfers with [[Lorenzo Amoruso]] and [[Marco Negri]] arriving in multimillion-pound deals. [[Paul Gascoigne]] also left the club, heading for [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]] in a £3.5m deal. Negri went on to become only the second player to score five goals in a Scottish Premier Division match, equalling [[Paul Sturrock]]'s record by netting all five goals in a 5–1 win over [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]].

The season began on 2 August with the first goal of the season scored by [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]]'s [[Kjell Olofsson]] as they drew 1–1 at newly promoted [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]]. The season ended on 9 May with [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]]'s [[Stevie Crawford]] netting a last-minute equaliser away to [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] to score the final goal of the season.

==Events==
* 23 August: [[Marco Negri]] equals [[Paul Sturrock]]'s record with five goals in one match in the 5–1 win over [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]]
* September: [[Darren Jackson (Scottish footballer)|Darren Jackson]] undergoes surgery for [[hydrocephalus]],<ref name="ill">{{cite news|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/other_sports/848867.stm|publisher=BBC Sport website|title=Winners against the odds|date=2000-07-20}}</ref> returning to action within three months<ref name="back">{{cite news|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/nol/ukfs_news/hi/newsid_80000/newsid_84200/84229.stm|title=The Scotland Squad|date=1998-05-03|publisher=BBC News & Sport website|access-date=2008-06-03}}</ref>
* 9 May: [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] win the title after a 2–0 home win over [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone F.C]]
